historical_references.reference: Arjitansh was a king of the Haihayas dynasty in the Magadha region of ancient India, around the 5th century BCE.
historical_references.context: Arjitansh is mentioned in Buddhist texts such as the Mahavamsa and the Dipavamsa, as a patron of Buddhism and a contemporary of Emperor Bimbisara of Magadha.

historical_references.reference: Arjitansh is also mentioned in Jain texts as a generous patron of Jain monks and scholars, contributing significantly to the growth of Jainism in Magadha around the 4th century BCE.
historical_references.context: Arjitansh is described as a just and pious ruler in Jain texts, who provided material support to the Jain monks and scholars, and is considered an important figure in the history of Jainism.
